subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 1: The Wonderful World of Science
central_question: How does curiosity, careful observation and a step-by-step scientific method help us ask questions and understand the world around us?
in_scope_units: Science as a way of thinking, observing and doing things to understand the world and the universe
Science everywhere — questions arising from nature, daily life, Earth, space, food, water, materials and motion
Science as an unending and connected jigsaw puzzle in which new discoveries may change earlier understanding
Overview of the themes and questions that the Grade 6 science book will explore
Finding answers through the pen example and the step-by-step scientific method
Scientific thinking in everyday work such as cooking, bicycle repair and electrical repair
Curiosity, asking why, teamwork and joyful exploration as habits of a science learner
banned_topics: Detailed classification of plants and animals from Chapter 2
Detailed nutrients and balanced diet from Chapter 3
Detailed properties of magnets from Chapter 4
Detailed measurement units and types of motion from Chapter 5

known_pitfalls.claim: Science is only a collection of facts that students must memorise.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter presents science as a way of thinking, observing, asking questions, testing guesses and analysing results.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only professional scientists use the scientific method.
known_pitfalls.correction: Anyone who asks a question, tests possible explanations and studies the result is working like a scientist.

known_pitfalls.claim: A scientific guess is accepted without testing.
known_pitfalls.correction: A possible answer must be tested through experiments or further observations, and the results must then be analysed.

recommended_example_progression: Use the pen-stops-writing example and Activity 1.1 to identify the stages of a scientific investigation.
Use Activity 1.2 to recognise scientific thinking in cooking, bicycle repair or electrical repair.
Use Activity 1.3 to frame a 'Why?' question and propose a way to find an answer.
Use the jigsaw-puzzle comparison to explain why new discoveries may lead to more questions or change earlier ideas.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: This introductory chapter has no separate 'Let us enhance our learning' exercise set; its practice is organised through Activities 1.1-1.3.
